title: Binding manifest expressions and recoverable error signatures for tool call params
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Call manifests expressed as JSON schemas are brittle when model outputs deviate slightly (typos, type mismatches, missing keys). Current behavior returns opaque validation errors which are hard for integrators to interpret and hard for runtime to recover from.

Goal: Define a compact "binding manifest" extension and an error/signature scheme that enables: (1) declarative runtime repairs (coercion, defaults, aliasing), (2) graded error severities (recoverable vs hard), (3) humanized error messages for SDKs, and (4) telemetry hooks for automatic quality regressions and rollout decisions. This ticket designs the format and implements the first runtime pass and agent-facing error mapping in the Node SDK.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Binding manifest syntax defined and documented (fits within existing call manifest JSON) with examples for defaults, aliases, coercion rules, and recoverable flags.
A2: Runtime implements ordered repair pipeline: normalize -> coerce -> alias -> default -> validate, with observable metrics for each step.
A3: Error responses include structured error_code, human_hint, severity (recoverable|hard), and suggest_fixes (where possible).
A4: Node SDK surfaces human_hint and suggest_fixes for developer console and CLI; unit tests cover 90% of repair scenarios and failure modes.
A5: Backward compatibility: manifests without binding extensions behave unchanged; feature gated by manifest v2 flag for rollouts.
technical_design:
Overview: We extend the existing JSON schema manifest with an optional top-level field "x_binding" per parameter that expresses lightweight expressions and repair strategies. The grammar is intentionally small: {"coerce_to": "string|number|boolean|array|object", "aliases": ["camelName", "snake_name"], "default_expr": "expr:\u003cjs-lite\u003e", "severity": "recoverable|hard", "examples": [...] }

Runtime: Implement a deterministic pipeline applied to model output before final validation: 1) Normalization (trim whitespace, unify quotes), 2) Type coercion (number strings -> number), 3) Alias resolution (map known alternative keys), 4) Default evaluation (evaluate safe exprs, e.g., timestamp now, empty array), 5) Strict schema validation. Each step emits a telemetry tag and a delta metric.

Error model: Errors emitted are flat objects with fields: error_code (string), severity (recoverable|hard), human_hint (short sentence), recover_actions (list), telemetry_tags (list). Example codes: BIND_COERCE_FAILED, BIND_MISSING_REQUIRED, BIND_ALIAS_APPLIED, BIND_DEFAULT_EVALUATED. SDKs map severity recoverable -> 200-style response with warnings header; hard -> 4xx style error.

Safety: default_expr only supports a restricted expression DSL (no arbitrary JS): safe ops (now(), substring(), parseInt, join, pick(path)), evaluated in a sandbox. Feature gated behind manifest_v2 flag.

Compatibility: If manifest lacks x_binding, runtime behaves as today. If manifest_v2 flag set, runtime will apply binding steps in configurable order and allow per-route toggles.

Telemetry: Add tags: binding.step=<step>, binding.param=<param>, binding.outcome=<applied|no-op|failed>, binding.lat_ms; these feed into Console rollout dashboard and quality alerts.
implementation_steps: 1) Spec PR: add detailed grammar and examples to confluence (link in links).
2) Implement binding parser in runtime core (C++) with a thin Node shim for SDK warnings.
3) Implement sandboxed evaluator for default_expr with deterministic primitives (Rust/Wasm module).
4) Add telemetry hooks and counters (Prometheus labels + tracing annotations).
5) Add Node SDK mapping: warnings header, human_hint surfaces, and CLI helper for suggest_fixes.
6) Integration tests: unit + synthetic prompts that exercise each repair path and failure modes.
7) Rollout: feature-flagged on runtime-1.22 -> gradual enable on non-production orgs -> full rollout after 2 weeks and metric stability.
notes: Design trade-offs: We intentionally avoid full expression Turing-completeness to limit audit surface and keep evaluation deterministic for caching/batching semantics.
Performance: binding steps must be extremely cheap to not regress token latency; heavy evals pushed to a wasm sandbox with per-call CPU budget.
Observability: each binding application should increment a counter to help derive the model drift signal for a given manifest.
Security: default_expr sandbox design will be reviewed by Security; no network or fs access allowed.
